verdict.summary: Register an app in any Mailchimp account and any Mailchimp user can authorize it the same day, with no review and no scopes to justify. The catches are all-or-nothing access (no granular scopes), tokens that never expire, a per-user data center you must look up, and a hard cap of 10 simultaneous connections per user.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Register an app, copy the client ID/secret, run the code flow against http://127.0.0.1. No verification step is documented.

timeToProd.assumes: An unlisted OAuth integration that reads and writes audiences and campaigns; a Marketplace listing via the Integration Partner Program is optional and needs 25+ active users first.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Neither OAuth page mentions any review, approval or user cap for registered apps.

prerequisites.item: A Mailchimp account (free is fine) to register the app
prerequisites.why: Apps are registered on the Registered Apps page inside a Mailchimp account.

prerequisites.item: A server-side backend that can hold the client secret
prerequisites.why: The code-for-token exchange uses the client_secret; Mailchimp's docs only describe the confidential server flow, not PKCE.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: PKCE support isn't mentioned in the pages we read.

prerequisites.item: A redirect URI reachable from the user's browser
prerequisites.why: Mailchimp redirects there with the code. HTTPS is strongly recommended but not enforced; http://127.0.0.1:3000/... is fine for local dev.

examples: (no scope parameter; the token grants full Marketing API access to the user's account)
scopeTiers.impact: One token reads and writes audiences, contacts, campaigns, reports and automations for the authorizing user. There's no way to request read-only access, so tell users plainly what your agent will touch.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Mailchimp's OAuth pages never mention scopes; an integration platform's docs say Mailchimp doesn't support granular scopes.

scopeTiers.impact: Gets you into the Mailchimp Marketplace and partner support. Requirements: current Marketing API, OAuth 2, and 25+ active users in the past 90 days. Not needed for users to connect.

steps.title: Sign in to a Mailchimp account
steps.detail: Use or create a Mailchimp account that will own the app registration (a company account rather than a personal one).

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: Go to Registered Apps, click Register An App, fill in name, description, company, app website and redirect URI, then Create. Copy the client_id and client_secret from the bottom of the page; the secret is shown only once.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The console URL redirected us to login.mailchimp.com (HTTP 302) on 2026-10-20.

steps.title: Implement the authorize redirect
steps.detail: Send users to https://login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=... and add a state parameter for CSRF protection.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: state isn't shown in Mailchimp's samples; adding it is our recommendation.

steps.title: Exchange the code for a token
steps.detail: POST to https://login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri and code. Store the access token encrypted; there's no refresh token.

steps.title: Look up the user's data center
steps.detail: Call the OAuth Metadata endpoint (https://login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/metadata) with the token to get the dc / api_endpoint, then call https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/. Store the dc with the token.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The endpoint exists: GET https://login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/metadata without a token returned HTTP 200 with {"error":"invalid_token"}. The current docs pages we read don't describe it (search snippets of Mailchimp docs say the token's data center comes from the OAuth Metadata endpoint), so the response fields dc / api_endpoint are from community usage.

steps.title: Build throttling and caching
steps.detail: Keep at most 10 concurrent requests per Mailchimp user, back off on 429 (and 403 without a body at high volume), cache slow-changing values, and use the Batch endpoint for anything that may exceed the 120-second timeout.

steps.title: Handle disconnects and revocation
steps.detail: On a 401 from a stored token, treat it as revoked and send the user back through authorization. On uninstall, delete the token and any sync configuration.

steps.title: Switch the redirect URI to production HTTPS
steps.detail: Edit the registered app to use your production HTTPS redirect URI and test a connection from a second Mailchimp account.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Whether one app can hold several redirect URIs isn't documented in the pages we read.

steps.title: Optionally apply to the Integration Partner Program
steps.detail: After 25+ active users in 90 days, apply for a Marketplace listing and partner support. Optional; users can connect without it.

agentCanDo: Implement the authorization code flow and token exchange
Resolve and store each user's data center via the metadata endpoint
Build a 10-connection-per-user request limiter with 429 backoff
Move long-running work to the Batch endpoint
Draft the app description and Partner Program application
humanMustDo: Sign in to Mailchimp and register the app
Copy and store the client secret (shown once)
Rotate the client secret if it's exposed
Apply to the Integration Partner Program if you want a listing

blockers.symptom: API calls return 404 or fail against https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/ with a valid OAuth token
blockers.cause: Marketing API calls go to a per-account data center subdomain (<dc>.api.mailchimp.com).
blockers.fix: Call the OAuth Metadata endpoint after the token exchange and use the returned dc / api_endpoint.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Prismatic's docs use a ${dc} placeholder in the base URL and say the data-center suffix is needed for routing; Mailchimp's current Fundamentals page only shows https://api.mailchimp.com/3.0/. The exact error on the wrong host wasn't verified.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, or a 403/429 with no JSON body under heavy load
blockers.cause: More than 10 simultaneous connections for the same Mailchimp user (the limit is per user, not per key or client).
blockers.fix: Serialize requests per user, cache slow-changing data, and use the Batch endpoint. Mailchimp says the limit can't be raised per customer.

blockers.cause: Tokens don't expire, so a 401 means the user revoked access or was removed from the account.
blockers.fix: Don't retry; mark the connection broken and ask the user to re-authorize.

blockers.symptom: All requests fail with 401 right after rotating the client secret
blockers.cause: Requests signed with the old secret fail once it's rotated.
blockers.fix: Deploy the new secret immediately after rotating in the app's Edit page.

blockers.symptom: Calls time out on large reports or list exports
blockers.cause: The Marketing API has a 120-second timeout on calls.
blockers.fix: Use pagination with fields/exclude_fields, or submit the work to the Batch endpoint (max 500 pending batch webhook events per user).

nuances.text: Access tokens have no expiry and there are no refresh tokens. A token is valid until the user revokes it or is removed from the account, so encrypt tokens at rest.
There are no granular scopes: a token can do anything the authorizing user can do in the Marketing API, including sending campaigns. Build your own guardrails before letting an agent send email.
Exceeding the limits can get your API access disabled, and there's no option to raise the 10-connection limit per customer.
Mailchimp isn't an OpenID Connect provider (no discovery document); identify the user from the metadata endpoint's account login details.
Mailchimp's free plan drops to 250 contacts and 500 sends a month in 2026, so many users' accounts will be small; that's an account limit, not an API restriction.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Third-party report; it doesn't mention API access, and we found no Mailchimp doc saying API access is restricted on free plans.

nuances.text: Mailchimp Transactional (formerly Mandrill) uses separate API keys, not this OAuth flow.
